prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the passenger in a sideswipe while changing lanes in Conroe, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1413; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my name on a recording, but I understand you need it for the file. You can use the claim reference you have.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were sitting at the time of the collision?

A: I was in the front passenger seat of my friend's sedan. He was driving.

Q: And where were you traveling?

A: We were on a multi-lane road in Conroe, Texas, heading toward the north side of town. It was late afternoon and traffic was moderate.

Q: Describe what happened.

A: My friend wanted to move into the left lane to make a turn. He checked his mirror and started to change lanes, and then a pickup on our left moved over into us. It sideswiped the back half of our car. We spun a little and then the car stopped against the curb.

Q: Did you hit anything inside the vehicle?

A: My head snapped to the right and then back. I didn't hit the window, but the seatbelt pulled hard across my chest and my neck jerked.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that evening. They said I had a neck strain and gave me muscle relaxers and told me to rest and use ice.

Q: How are you feeling now?

A: Still stiff in the neck, and I get a dull ache when I turn my head to check traffic. Sleeping has been harder than usual.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: Not yet, but I've been taking it easy and I may need to see a physical therapist if it doesn't improve.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to make sure my medical bills are handled properly.
